Subject: Kickoff + hands-on prompt workshop — StackWalk POC

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The product team at StackWalk is excited to move to a hands-on POC. We'd like to schedule a kickoff + prompt review workshop where we:
- walk through our prompt inventory and example conversations
- align on structured output requirements (JSON schema)
- run a short routing/load test against a representative prompt mix

Our initial preference is a 2-hour block the week of Oct 4th, ideally in the morning PT. Key participants: myself, Matt (ML lead), and a product PM.

Could you propose 2-3 time options and any prep you need (prompt list, guardrail checklist, runbook)?

Appreciate it — Claire

--
Claire Huang
Head of Product, StackWalk
claire@stackwalk.ai

- Tue Oct 5, 09:00–11:00 PT
- Wed Oct 6, 08:00–10:00 PT
- Thu Oct 7, 10:00–12:00 PT (preferred if you need extra time)

Prep we need from you:
- prompt inventory (sample 30–50 prompts; spreadsheet is perfect)
- examples of expected structured outputs / sample JSON schema

I'll loop in Ben (solutions) and Karthik (technical lead) to confirm load-test capacity and whether we should run a 20-minute burstload within the session. Also confirm your preferred region (we can run in us-west or eu-west).

If those slots don't work, tell me two times that do and we'll reschedule.

Grace / team — quick ops note:
- We can support a 20-minute burstload during the workshop (single-node quantized variant + a fallback to a smaller model).
- Recommended traffic shape: 50 concurrent short prompts (avg 60 tokens) to exercise KV cache and routing.
- For routing, bring any country or tenant rules — we'll demo Smart Routing and automatic fallback.

I'll prepare a short loadtest harness and a monitoring dashboard for the session. Monica, can you prepare a one-slide CS checklist (SLOs, success criteria) so we can capture acceptance?

Ben

Thanks — a few quick technical asks so we can prep templates:
1) Schema: if you can provide a representative JSON schema (or a couple of samples), we'll prep structured-output validators and a small transformer to map model outputs into your storage format.
2) Prompt inventory: include labels for intent (e.g., support_reply, summarization, reranking) and expected token distributions.
3) Guardrails: any forbidden content or PII rules we should enforce client-side vs. server-side?

Proposed agenda (we'll refine in the invite):
- 0:00–0:20 Intro + goals
- 0:20–0:50 Prompt inventory walkthrough
- 0:50–1:20 Structured output design + validator demo
- 1:20–1:40 Live routing demo + failover
- 1:40–2:00 Burstload run + monitoring review

I can own the validator demo and the runbook for structured outputs. Ben will own loadtest harness. Grace — do you want the final invite to include the 2-hour lab with a 20-min loadtest block at the end?

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
